sections.title: NRN/CNTRL PLAINS INTO UPPER GREAT LAKES
sections.text: QUASI-ZONAL FLOW REGIME WILL EXIST TODAY ACROSS THE N-CNTRL CONUS WITH SEVERAL EMBEDDED VORTICITY MAXIMA TRANSLATING EWD ACROSS THE REGION. AT THE SURFACE...TWO BOUNDARIES WILL LIKELY SERVE AS THE FOCUS FOR MORE CONCENTRATED TSTM ACTIVITY THROUGH THE DIURNAL HEATING CYCLE. THE NRN-MOST IS CURRENTLY TRAILING SWWD FROM LOW PRESSURE OVER LAKE SUPERIOR THROUGH CNTRL MN TO SECONDARY LOW PRESSURE OVER CNTRL SD. THE NRN EXTENSION OF THIS BOUNDARY WILL PROGRESS EWD THROUGH THE UP OF MI AND MORE SEWD/SWD ACROSS NRN WI AND SRN MN. FARTHER S...A DEEPENING SURFACE LOW OVER S-CNTRL NEB WILL ANCHOR AN ARCING COMPOSITE OUTFLOW/WARM FRONTAL BOUNDARY OVER CNTRL/ERN NEB INTO WRN IA AND NWRN MO. THE RESIDUAL EFFECT OF ONGOING...MID MO VALLEY MCS ON RESULTANT AIR MASS DESTABILIZATION REMAINS UNCERTAIN. HOWEVER...LATEST MESOSCALE MODEL GUIDANCE IS RATHER CONSISTENT IN SUGGESTING THAT THE COMBINATION OF 70-75 F DEWPOINTS ALONG IMMEDIATE COOL SIDE OF OUTFLOW BOUNDARY/WARM FRONT AND STRONG DIABATIC HEATING TO THE S WILL CONTRIBUTE TO AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES OF 2500-3500+ J/KG FROM CNTRL NEB INTO THE LOWER MO VALLEY. LESSER INSTABILITY IS FORECAST FURTHER TO THE N --I.E. CNTRL/SRN SD INTO SRN MN-- INVOF NR

sections.title: SERN U.S
sections.text: A HOT AND VERY MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER WILL ONCE AGAIN RESULT IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF A MODERATELY UNSTABLE AIR MASS TODAY WITH AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES OF 1500-3000 J/KG. THE PRESENCE OF A WEAK SYNOPTIC BOUNDARY ACROSS SRN GA NWWD INTO NRN MS AND DEVELOPING SEA BREEZE CIRCULATIONS WILL SERVE TO FOCUS DIURNALLY ENHANCED PULSE-TYPE STORM CLUSTERS. THE MAIN THREAT WITH THESE STORMS WILL BE LOCALLY STRONG WIND GUSTS. ..MEAD/SMITH.. 08/02/2010

sections.title: NEB/IA THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT
sections.text: AN OVERNIGHT MCS CONTINUES TO WEAKEN OVER IA WITH THE REMAINING CONVECTION ASSOCIATED WITH LOW-LEVEL WAA OVER NE MO AND MIDLEVEL WAA OVER E CENTRAL NEB. THE NE MO CONVECTION MAY PERSIST FOR A FEW MORE HOURS AS CONVECTION DEVELOPS SEWD ALONG THE INSTABILITY GRADIENT JUST W OF THE MS RIVER...THOUGH WEAKENING OF THE WSWLY LLJ SEGMENT ACROSS NRN MO BY EARLY AFTERNOON SUGGESTS THAT THESE STORMS SHOULD NOT INTENSIFY SUBSTANTIALLY. THE OUTFLOW TRAILING SWWD FROM THE REMNANT MCS HAS REINFORCED THE BAROCLINIC ZONE NEAR THE KS/NEB BORDER...E OF A REMNANT LEE CYCLONE. THE CONSOLIDATED BOUNDARY SHOULD MOVE NWD INTO ERN NEB THIS AFTERNOON AS SURFACE HEATING MODIFIES THE COLD POOL...AND ALSO REDUCES CONVECTIVE INHIBITION ON THE NOSE OF THE VERY HOT/DEEPLY MIXED BOUNDARY LAYER INTO NRN KS. THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT IS EXPECTED LATE THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING ALONG THE BOUNDARY IN ERN NEB/WRN IA. A CORRIDOR OF LOW-MID 70S BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS WILL CONTRIBUTE TO STRONG INSTABILITY /MLCAPE NEAR 3000 J PER KG/ ALONG THE OUTFLOW/WARM FRONT THIS AFTERNOON...BENEATH A BELT OF 35-50 KT WLY FLOW ALOFT. THE ENVIRONMENT WILL SUPPORT SUPERCELLS WITH THE INITIAL STORM DEVELOPMENT...WITH THE POTENTIAL FOR A TOR

sections.title: NRN PLAINS THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING
sections.text: A MUDDLED SURFACE PATTERN EXISTS ACROSS THE NRN PLAINS WITH ONE FRONTAL SEGMENT EXTENDING WSWWD FROM E CENTRAL MN INTO CENTRAL SD...WHILE OTHER MORE DIFFUSE BOUNDARY SEGMENTS AND WEAK OUTFLOWS EXIST FARTHER N INTO WRN ND. THE MAIN BELT OF WLYS ALOFT WILL RESIDE OVER ND TODAY AS AN EMBEDDED SHORTWAVE TROUGH EJECTS EWD OVER NRN ND AND THE ADJACENT PRAIRIE PROVINCES. DESPITE THE STRONGER FLOW ALOFT AND ASSOCIATED DEEP-LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR...INSTABILITY WILL BE LIMITED ACROSS ND AS A RESULT OF LOW-LEVEL DRYING AND POOR LAPSE RATES ABOVE 500 MB. AN ISOLATED LOW-TOPPED SUPERCELL CANNOT BE RULED OUT...BUT THE SEVERE STORM THREAT IS TOO LIMITED TO WARRANT A SLIGHT RISK FARTHER S INTO SD...CLOUD BREAKS AND LINGERING BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS NEAR 70 F WILL SUPPORT MODERATE INSTABILITY ALONG THE QUASI-STATIONARY FRONTAL SEGMENT. CONVECTIVE INHIBITION IS WEAKER OVER SD ALONG THE N EDGE OF THE SUBTROPICAL MOISTURE PLUME...COMPARED TO THE WARMER MIDLEVEL TEMPERATURES FARTHER TO THE S. THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT APPEARS PROBABLE THIS AFTERNOON ALONG THE FRONT WHERE INSTABILITY AND VERTICAL SHEAR WILL BE SUFFICIENT FOR A FEW SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS. ..THOMPSON/S

sections.title: DAKOTAS
sections.text: WHILE LOW LEVEL SHEAR IS WEAK AND CHAOTIC...DEEP LAYER SHEAR OF 30-40KT WOULD SUPPORT SOME STORM ORGANIZATION. WITH STRONG HEATING ALONG WITH AVAILABLE LOW LEVEL MOISTURE...SBCAPES HAVE CLIMBED TO AROUND 3000 J/KG FROM SRN ND SWD THRU ERN SD. HAVE EXPANDED THE RISK OF SCATTERED STRONG/SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS NWD INTO SRN ND.

sections.title: NRN VT/NERN NY
sections.text: SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS HAVE DEVELOPED ACROSS THIS AREA WITH AFTERNOON HEATING. MLCAPES TO 1000 J/KG AND STEEP LOW/MID LAPSE RATES HAVE LED TO A FEW STRONG THUNDERSTORMS INCLUDING ISOLATED HAIL. WITH LITTLE UPPER SUPPORT STORMS SHOULD QUICKLY DECREASE IN NUMBER AND INTENSITY BY SUNSET.

sections.title: NEB/IA
sections.text: LITTLE CHANGE IN THIS AREA. STILL A QUESTION AS TO H0W SOON BEFORE SUNSET WILL SURFACE BASED INITIATION CAN OCCUR GIVEN THE WARM AIR ALOFT. HOWEVER WITH THE INCREASED LOW LEVEL JET AFTER 00Z...SEVERE THUNDERSTORM POTENTIAL EXPECTED TO INCREASE ACROSS MUCH OF ERN NEB INTO IA. ..HALES.. 08/02/2010 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1132 AM CDT MON AUG 02 2010/
